simplified:
For many years, I made computer art and geometric art using a piece of paper on plans. I wrote the line and sometimes built the machines. I shared my work on social media, thinking people might enjoy the soft sounds and presses. But no one really noticed. One day, someone gave me a chocolate 3D printer machine. I filled it with paint and made a big mess. I wanted to make some points, but they were not in order. Some people got angry, some felt sorry for the machine, and some even danced to it. Mostly, people were angry.

 I made a piece called “Bad day at the round shop.” I found out I could make different experiences with just a machine and pen and paper. People got very angry and gently shouted at me, saying things like "I hope your bed is warm." My videos started getting millions of views and many replies. People asked me to make mazes. I thought, how can I mess up a hunt? I made one that went right past the door. I had to learn the rules of this art form. Each piece had to be about 12 to 15 seconds long and go quickly. I tried to hide my mistakes and make the endings surprising. I promised people enjoyable returns, but then I would trouble them. Many thought my work was about AI. One video went viral, and people watched my 17-second video for 200,000 hours. I got so many notices that my phone kept dying. In the end, rules can be good for making art, but I felt like I was just sharing my own work, which I didn’t like. So, I took a break. If you see something on that bothers you a little, it might have been me. Thank you.
